_notes: The orders told apart (DESIGN §9.4b). Each profile is what makes a house of that order a different neighbour: its own words for itself, its own people beyond the roles every institute fills, the favours only it does, and the lines the sheet uses when one is given. The id is the institute's (institutes.json); houseOrder is the house's (houses.json). Titles and structures are the real ones: a Dominican priory under a prior, a Franciscan friary under a guardian, an Augustinian priory under a prior; provinces under a provincial; the Dominican family of friars, cloistered nuns, apostolic sisters, and lay Dominicans; the Franciscan family of Friars Minor, Capuchins, Conventuals, Third Order Regular, Poor Clares, and Secular Franciscans; the Augustinian friars, contemplative nuns, and the Recollects.

orders.family: the friars, the cloistered nuns who were there before the friars were, the apostolic sisters who taught half the diocese, and the lay Dominicans who meet in a parish hall on a Tuesday
orders.governance: a priory elects its prior for three years, the province elects its provincial for four, and the whole order is governed by chapters that have been arguing since 1220 and consider that the method
orders.habit: white, with a black cappa over it in choir and a rosary at the belt; a Dominican in a parish is recognised from the back pew

people.line: prior of the priory, elected by the house, and it shows
lector of the house, who has read everything and expects you to have read some of it

people.title: Br.
people.line: a student brother, three years from ordination, who preaches better than he knows

lines.confessor: {who} will take the Saturday box from now on. He hears a confession the way he reads a text, and the people who want to be understood rather than comforted find their way to his side.
lines.mission: {house} will preach the mission: five nights of doctrine preached as if it were news, and a Wednesday confessional that runs past eleven.
lines.course: {who} will teach the course in the hall: six Thursday nights on the Creed, article by article, to people who did not know they wanted it. The hall is fuller the sixth night than the first.
lines.opinion: {who} has written you four pages, with footnotes, that say what you said in language the chancery cannot call an opinion. You put it in the file. It is read.
lines.vicar: The provincial has assigned {who} to the parish. He keeps his hours and his habit, preaches on Sundays in a register the parish has not heard, and argues with you at dinner, which you come to look forward to.

orders.blurb: Preachers by rule and readers by habit: a house that will teach your parish, argue with you at its table, and put a stand of yours in writing the chancery cannot wave away.

orders.family: the Friars Minor, the Capuchins with the beards, the Conventuals with the black habit, the Third Order Regular, the Poor Clares behind their grille, and the Secular Franciscans who wear the cord under a suit
orders.governance: a friary under a guardian, a province under a minister provincial, and a rule that owns nothing and a province that owns the friary, which they have been explaining for eight hundred years
orders.habit: brown, with a white cord and three knots; the city knows the habit before it knows the collar

people.line: guardian of the friary, which is the word they use instead of superior, on purpose

people.title: Br.
people.line: the brother who runs the kitchen, not a priest, and the best-known man of the house
the friar in the box on Saturdays, whose line runs past the last pew

lines.confessor: {who} will drive out for the Saturday hours from now on. He is easy to confess to, which the people notice by the second week, and the line is out the door by Advent.
lines.mission: {house} will preach the mission: five nights of the mercy of God from a man who has slept in a shelter, and a church that fills with people who have not been inside one in years.
lines.kitchen: {who} will run a kitchen out of the hall on Tuesdays, from now on: a hot meal for whoever comes, the friars' own volunteers, and a line down the block that the neighbours will have opinions about.
lines.mercy: The friary has taken the parish's winter: the coal fund, the Christmas baskets, the families you have been carrying on the parish's money. They ask for nothing back and mean it.
lines.vicar: The provincial has assigned {who} to the parish. He gives away his stipend, keeps the kitchen door open, and is loved by the people you find hardest, which is instructive.

orders.blurb: The poor and the door: a house whose brother in the kitchen is better known than its guardian, and which will bring your parish's poor into your own hall.

orders.family: the friars, the contemplative nuns, the Augustinian Recollects who went their own way in 1588 and kept the name, and the sisters who run schools under the same rule
orders.governance: a priory under a prior, a province under a prior provincial, and a rule older than any of them, written by a bishop of Hippo for a house of clerics who were to have one heart and one soul in God, which is the line over the door
orders.habit: black, with a leather belt and a hood; in the school they wear a collar and the boys call every one of them Father

people.line: prior of the priory, who sits at the head of a table that is the whole point of the house
headmaster of the order's school, who knows every family in the diocese with money and most without
pastor of the parish they have held a hundred years, and the fourth of his order in that chair

lines.confessor: {who} will take the Saturday box from now on. He hears the parish the way he hears the boys at the school: without surprise, and without letting anyone off.
lines.mission: {house} will preach the mission: five nights on the restless heart, from a man who has read the Confessions more times than you have read anything.
lines.school_place: {who} has found a place at the school for the family from the parish: the tuition halved, the rest found, and a boy in a blazer on the first Monday of September who did not expect to be.
lines.common_table: You have a place at the priory's table on Thursdays, from now on. Dinner at six, the prior at the head, the argument of the week, and nobody asks you how the parish is going unless you want to say.
lines.vicar: The provincial has assigned {who} to the parish. He goes home to the priory for dinner most nights, and after a month asks whether you would like to come, which is the order's way of saying you are theirs too.

orders.blurb: The common table: a house that keeps a school and a parish and a dinner at six, and which will give a priest with no community a chair at theirs.
